beats.trigger: ## Security
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: You can't tell if your agent is safe from its output.
beats.got: Nobody can sign off on an agent by looking at what it says, so some separate check is needed.

beats.trigger: Prework covers personal skills and agent risk layered on normal security.
beats.got: nothing new. It's a reading list I haven't read, with no cost attached.

beats.trigger: **Distinguish** compliant, violating and "I can't tell" for each rule
beats.got: Rules get three verdicts, not two. The rest of the list is jargon.

beats.trigger: Name what you'd want to check before letting this near a real stakeholder.
beats.got: I should say what worries me before it touches real people. That one is a fair question.

beats.trigger: A tool call is text crossing a boundary into action.
beats.got: The agent writes text and software turns it into actions, so a bad instruction becomes a bad action. No cost or risk figure given.

beats.trigger: Would you bet your job on it being safe?
beats.got: This asks whether I'd put my own name on it. That is the board question.

beats.trigger: Classical software security is a risk-based practice, and the software it protects is deterministic: same input, same output.
beats.got: Old security assumed software behaves the same way every time.

beats.trigger: One passing test is one sample.
beats.got: A pass today proves little, because the same agent can answer differently tomorrow. That is an audit problem I understand.

beats.trigger: Scope (give the agent less). Split (two agents, different trust levels). Filter (post-process output). Gate (human approves). Review (a second agent judges).
beats.got: There are five standard fixes. A human approval gate is the one I'd trust. The second-agent review sounds circular.

beats.trigger: the residual risk is X; if Y happens, we made it less likely, not prevented it.
beats.got: A residual-risk statement accepted on the record is something I could take to the board.

beats.trigger: Scope it down far enough and the system is safe and useless.
beats.got: Safety and usefulness trade against each other, and someone has to sign for where the line sits.

beats.trigger: Expect it to cost you a feature.
beats.got: The cheapest control is not connecting the system, and it has a real price. The slide admits that up front.

beats.trigger: Damn, this is complex stuff.
beats.got: nothing new. It's a pep talk with no figure in it.

beats.trigger: a skill is a reusable check you run again instead of re-prompting from memory.
beats.got: A skill is a saved check that can be rerun. That sounds like a control procedure, which I understand.

beats.trigger: Read the first few rows: they show which rules files can check and which need judgment, context, or a standing evidence check.
beats.got: Some policy rules can be checked automatically and some need a person. That's useful, but it isn't my material (no finance policy is involved).

beats.trigger: the customer your CEO would not want named in a transcript.
beats.got: I'm supposed to name what we can't leak. I can do that, but it's a vague step.

beats.trigger: Expect many questions; the agent keeps probing both lenses over several rounds.
beats.got: This is twenty-two minutes of Q&A, and I can't see the payoff yet.

beats.trigger: "You choose. Optimise for what I can't steer."
beats.got: I can delegate the details to the agent and keep the judgment calls. That I can do.

beats.trigger: Run `ls .claude/skills/agent-audit/` to confirm.
beats.got: This is mechanical setup that belongs to IT.

beats.trigger: The reusable check carries the judgment about what matters in this system
beats.got: The value is the check our own people shape, not the tool. That is not a licence purchase.

beats.trigger: The goal is the loop (assess, mitigate, reassess residual), not a clean bill of health.
beats.got: Nobody promises me a clean result. Honest, at least.

beats.trigger: Type `/` and look for `/agent-audit` in the autocomplete list.
beats.got: nothing new. I type a slash and look for a name.

beats.trigger: Expect the reusable check to find things you did not think about, and to leave things "I can't tell" you thought were settled.
beats.got: The audit finds new gaps and also reopens things I thought were closed. That is what an auditor does.

beats.trigger: The uncomfortable feeling is the evidence.
beats.got: Feeling uneasy is being treated as proof. I want a number, not a feeling.

beats.trigger: The risk remains. That is expected. Name it, accept it on record, and stop there.
beats.got: One risk mitigated, the remainder written down and accepted on record. That is a controls log I recognise.

beats.trigger: The narrow question the expert can answer is sitting in the report. Walk in with that.
beats.got: When the report can't settle it, I take a narrow question to legal or security with the evidence attached.

beats.trigger: Risk control, done for every risk you found, separates a prototype from a production agent.
beats.got: We did one risk, and production means doing all of them. There's no cost estimate for that, and it's the number I need.

beats.trigger: The reusable check is the expert in the room, and it carries to the next agent.
beats.got: We now have a repeatable check and a report holding the evidence and decisions.

beats.trigger: *"that residual is too vague, name the file or behaviour."*
beats.got: The agent writes rules for next time, and I push back when they're vague.

beats.trigger: A skill is not a deployed service and does not settle ownership.
beats.got: Skills can be handed to colleagues, but they don't answer who owns them. A fair caveat.

beats.trigger: Mitigations add to security controls, never replace them.
beats.got: Agent fixes sit on top of existing controls. That is fine with me.

beats.trigger: Without the two sentences, you'll be writing them while the rest of the room is already comparing detectors. Your call.
beats.got: There's homework before the next module, framed as a nudge.

beats.trigger: Read Mata v. Avianca (2023) and Deloitte Australia / DEWR report (2025) in the lecture.
beats.got: Two real cases where unchecked AI output cost someone. The Deloitte one involves money, so I'd read that.

take_homes: You cannot get certainty on an agent. You run assess, mitigate, name the residual, decide, and write the residual down on the record.
The cheapest control is the door you don't open, and it costs a feature. Scoping down is a business decision someone signs for.
The saved check is something our own people build and rerun, and I still need IT and legal to sign off on the hard calls.

monday.move: Ask IT and legal what rules would apply before any finance data goes near an agent. Then ask my controller to list what a variance-commentary agent would read and write, and what it could leak.
monday.who: Controller and the head of IT
monday.stop_condition: IT has not approved the tool for finance data, or no one can give me a cost per month and a named residual risk.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data. I also still have no cost, payback or per-seat number.

misconception.why: The module said the value sits in the reusable check our own people shape, not in the tool. That is closer to a capability than a licence. It was never costed, though, so I'm only half moved.

one_line: Good on honest risk: it names the residual and admits that closing a door costs a feature. But it gives me no cost or payback figure, and the exercises weren't on my material.
